question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?  (RRB NTPC CBT-I (24/07/2021) Shift 2)
options: Creating innovative business models to increase the wealth of its member countries
Providing loans to countries that have trouble meeting their international payments
Assisting mainly low and middle income countries to effectively manage their economies
Monitoring the financial and economic policies of its member countries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Creating innovative business models to increase the wealth of its member countries

Explanation:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is an international organization that promotes global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and international trade. Its core functions include providing loans to countries facing balance of payments problems, monitoring economic and financial policies of member countries, and offering technical assistance to low and middle-income countries. However, creating innovative business models to increase the wealth of its member countries is not a function of the IMF. This role is typically performed by private sector entities or development banks. The IMF focuses on macroeconomic stability and policy advice rather than business model innovation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Primary mission of IMF → Ensure global monetary cooperation and financial stability.
☛ IMF established in → 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference.
☛ IMF provides loans to → Countries facing balance of payments crises.
☛ IMF monitors → Economic and financial policies of member countries.
☛ Difference between IMF and World Bank → IMF focuses on monetary stability; World Bank provides loans for development projects.

question: The final approval of Five year plans in India is done by: (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)
options: Planning Commission
Reserve Bank of India
Finance Ministry
National Development Council
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Development Council

Explanation:
The final approval of Five-Year Plans in India is given by the National Development Council (NDC). The NDC is a quasi-constitutional body chaired by the Prime Minister. It includes all Chief Ministers of states, administrators of Union Territories, and members of the Union Cabinet. The NDC was established on August 6, 1952. It reviews the draft plans prepared by the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog) and provides the final seal of approval. The Planning Commission only drafts the plan, while the NDC gives the final nod. The Reserve Bank and Finance Ministry are involved only in financial aspects, not in overall plan approval.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the National Development Council established? → August 6, 1952
☛ Who chairs the NDC? → Prime Minister
☛ Which body used to draft Five-Year Plans? → Planning Commission
☛ Who represents states in NDC? → Chief Ministers
☛ Which body replaced the Planning Commission? → NITI Aayog

question: Government of India accounts are kept in three parts. Which of the following is NOT one of the three? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: Public Account
Cooperative fund
Consolidated Fund
Contingency Fund
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cooperative fund

Explanation:
The Government of India accounts are divided into three parts: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, and Public Account. This classification is defined under Articles 266 and 267 of the Indian Constitution. The Consolidated Fund includes all government revenues and expenditures, such as taxes and other receipts. The Contingency Fund is used for urgent expenses during emergencies. The Public Account holds other monies like deposits and provident funds. Among the options, Cooperative fund is not part of the government accounts; it pertains to cooperative societies.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many parts are Government of India accounts divided into? → Three
☛ Under which article is the Consolidated Fund defined? → Article 266
☛ What is the purpose of the Contingency Fund? → For emergency expenses
☛ What is kept in the Public Account? → Deposits and provident funds
☛ Under which article is the Contingency Fund defined? → Article 267

solution_hi:

Explanation:
भारत सरकार के खातों को तीन भागों में रखा जाता है: समेकित निधि, आकस्मिक निधि, और सार्वजनिक खाता। यह वर्गीकरण भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 266 और 267 में परिभाषित है। समेकित निधि में सरकार की सारी आय और व्यय शामिल होते हैं, जिसमें कर और अन्य प्राप्तियाँ आती हैं। आकस्मिक निधि का उपयोग आपात स्थितियों में तत्काल खर्च के लिए किया जाता है। सार्वजनिक खाता में जमा, भविष्य निधि आदि जैसी अन्य राशियाँ रखी जाती हैं। विकल्पों में दिया गया सहकारी निधि सरकारी खातों का हिस्सा नहीं है, बल्कि यह सहकारी समितियों से संबंधित होता है।

question: Which of the following is NOT correct in the context of PSUs and their year of establishment? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/03/2021) Shift 2)

Explanation:
The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was established in the year 1948, not 1958. It is India's first multipurpose river valley project. question: According to the 2014 Rangarajan Committee regarding national poverty lines in India, which of the following statements is correct? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (09/03/2021) Shift 2)
options: A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹872 living in the rural areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹2,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor.
A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,272 living in the rural areas should be considered poor.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A person who has a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of less than ₹1,407 living in the urban areas should be considered poor.

Explanation:
The Rangarajan Committee (2014) revised the methodology for estimating poverty lines in India. It recommended a monthly per capita consumption expenditure of ₹1,407 for rural areas and ₹2,407 for urban areas. This expenditure is based on the cost of basic needs like food, education, health, and housing. Option 1 (₹872) is incorrect for rural areas, Option 2 (₹2,407) is the correct urban threshold but not the one listed, and Option 4 (₹1,272) is also incorrect. Hence, the correct statement is that a person in urban areas with expenditure below ₹1,407 is considered poor.

☛ Which previous committee's norms did the Rangarajan Committee revise? → Tendulkar Committee

question: Who presented the first Union Budget of Independent India? (RRB JE CE (28/08/2019) Shift 1 CBT 2)
options: N.K. Chanda
John Mathai
R.K. Shanmukham Chetty
Morarji Desai
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is R.K. Shanmukham Chetty

Explanation:
The first Union Budget of independent India was presented on 26 November 1947 by the then Finance Minister R.K. Shanmukham Chetty. This was an interim budget covering the period from 15 August 1947 to 31 March 1948. He managed the country's economic situation after independence and focused on agriculture, industry, and infrastructure in the budget. John Mathai and Morarji Desai later became Finance Ministers. N.K. Chanda was a civil servant.

question: ________ is a floor with fixed significance, at which point the value of the probability is fixed. (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Numeric Probability Floor
Multi Planting Floor
Nominal Floor
Assimilation Floor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Assimilation Floor

Explanation:
Assimilation Floor is a statistical concept that represents a fixed value of probability for an event. It is the point at which the probability value is determined and does not increase further. This concept is used in probability theory and decision theory, where it indicates a type of threshold. Other options like Numeric Probability Floor or Nominal Floor are not accurate in this context. Assimilation Floor is applied in situations where probability stabilizes at a certain level, aiding decision-making. This concept is important for exams related to statistics and reasoning. It helps in understanding how probabilities can have a fixed significance in various scenarios.

question: When was the restructuring of public distribution system as a targeted public distribution system?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 2)

Earlier, PDS was universal and had no targeting. Under TPDS, BPL families receive highly subsidized food grains, while APL families receive lower subsidies. question: Which of the following is an example of a natural monopoly?  (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Malls
Apple store in delhi
Bookshop
Railways
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Railways

Explanation:
A natural monopoly occurs when a single firm can efficiently serve the entire market demand due to high infrastructure costs or economies of scale. Railways are a classic example because laying tracks, maintenance, and operating trains require massive capital investment. It is economically unfeasible for two competing railway companies to build separate tracks. Therefore, the government often owns or regulates railways. Other options like malls, Apple store, and bookshop are not natural monopolies as multiple competitors can easily enter the market. Natural monopolies often exist in utility sectors such as water supply, electricity grids, and railways.

question: Which period in India's demographic history is marked by a sharp decline in mortality and persistently high fertility rates? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Phase II (1921–1951)
Phase IV (1981–2001)
Phase I (1901–1921)
Phase III (1951–1981)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Phase III (1951–1981)

Explanation:
The third phase of India's demographic transition (1951-1981) is characterized by a sharp decline in mortality while fertility remained high. After independence, improvements in healthcare, control of infectious diseases, and better nutrition led to a drop in death rates. However, family planning programs had limited impact, keeping birth rates high. This caused rapid population growth, often termed the 'population explosion'. India's population increased from 36 crores in 1951 to 68 crores in 1981 during this phase.

question: Uninterrupted and seamless chain of Input Tax Credit (ITC) is a mechanism to avoid cascading of taxes in which of the following taxes? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: GST
Angel tax
Equalisation levy
Countervailing duty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GST

Explanation:
GST is an indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services across India. Its key feature is the uninterrupted chain of Input Tax Credit (ITC), which eliminates the cascading effect of taxes. Cascading means 'tax on tax', which was common in the old tax system. Under ITC, businesses can adjust the tax paid on inputs against the tax payable on output. This ensures that tax is levied only on the final consumer, not on intermediaries. Angel tax, equalisation levy, and countervailing duty do not have such a chain of ITC. Therefore, GST is the only tax that avoids cascading through ITC.

☛ What is the full form of ITC? → Input Tax Credit
☛ Which tax eliminates cascading of taxes? → GST
☛ Which country first implemented GST? → France
☛ When was GST implemented in India? → 1 July 2017

question: Privatisation was a key pillar of the New Economic Policy of 1991. Which of the following is NOT a form of privatisation?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (18/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Strategic sale
Disinvestment
Sovereign borrowing
Asset monetisation
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sovereign borrowing

Explanation:
Privatisation was a key pillar of India's New Economic Policy of 1991. Privatisation involves reducing government ownership and control of public sector enterprises. Strategic sale refers to selling a significant stake along with management control to a private entity. Disinvestment involves selling government shares partially or fully. Asset monetisation involves generating revenue from underutilised government assets. However, sovereign borrowing is when a government borrows from international financial markets in foreign currency. This is a form of public debt, not a method of privatisation. Hence, sovereign borrowing is not a form of privatisation.

☛ Disinvestment is → Sale of government stake in PSUs
☛ Strategic sale → Sale with transfer of management control
☛ Asset monetisation → Generating income from government assets
☛ Sovereign borrowing → Government borrowing in foreign currency

1991 में भारत ने गंभीर भुगतान संतुलन संकट का सामना किया। इस स्थिति से निपटने के लिए भारत सरकार ने आर्थिक सुधारों की शुरुआत की, जिसमें अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मुद्रा कोष (IMF) ने महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। IMF ने भारत को संरचनात्मक समायोजन ऋण प्रदान किया और सुधारों को लागू करने में सहायता की। इन सुधारों में उदारीकरण, निजीकरण और वैश्वीकरण शामिल थे, जिन्हें LPG नीति के नाम से जाना जाता है। IMF के समर्थन से भारत ने अपनी अर्थव्यवस्था को खोला और विदेशी निवेश को आकर्षित किया, जिससे संकट से उबरने में मदद मिली।

question: Which of the following is a window provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for banks to borrow overnight funds at a higher interest rate than the repo rate? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Open market operation
Standing deposit facility
Marginal standing facility
Off-budget financing
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marginal standing facility

Explanation:
The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) is a window provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for banks to borrow overnight funds at a higher interest rate than the repo rate. It was introduced in the monetary policy of 2011-12. Under MSF, banks can borrow funds from their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) portfolio. The MSF rate is generally 25 basis points above the repo rate. This facility helps banks meet their short-term liquidity shortages. Other options: Open market operation involves purchase/sale of government securities, Standing deposit facility allows banks to deposit funds at a rate lower than repo rate, and Off-budget financing refers to borrowing by government outside the budget.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What is the full form of MSF? → Marginal Standing Facility
☛ How much higher is MSF rate than repo rate? → 25 basis points (0.25%)
☛ From which portfolio do banks borrow under MSF? → SLR portfolio
☛ In which year was MSF introduced? → 2011-12
☛ Which facility allows overnight borrowing at a rate higher than repo? → MSF

Explanation:
भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (RBI) द्वारा बैंकों को रेपो दर से अधिक ब्याज दर पर रातों-रात धन उधार लेने के लिए सीमांत स्थायी सुविधा (MSF) प्रदान की जाती है। इसे 2011-12 की मौद्रिक नीति में शामिल किया गया था। MSF के तहत बैंक अपने सांविधिक तरलता अनुपात (SLR) पोर्टफोलियो से धन जुटा सकते हैं। MSF दर आमतौर पर रेपो दर से 25 आधार अंक अधिक होती है। यह सुविधा बैंकों को अल्पकालिक तरलता की कमी को पूरा करने में मदद करती है। अन्य विकल्प: मुक्त बाजार संचालन सरकारी प्रतिभूतियों की खरीद-बिक्री है, स्थायी जमा सुविधा बैंकों को रेपो दर से कम दर पर धन जमा करने की सुविधा है, और बजट से बाहर वित्तपोषण सरकार द्वारा बजट के बाहर उधार लेना है।

question: The 1991 reforms led to major tax policy changes to boost efficiency and compliance. Which tax reform, implemented in 2017, aimed to unify India's indirect tax structure? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: VAT
GST
Service Tax
Excise Duty
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is GST

Explanation:
GST (Goods and Services Tax) was implemented in India on 1 July 2017. It unified multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, service tax, VAT, and others into a single system. The reform aimed to create a common national market, simplify compliance, and increase tax revenue. The 1991 economic reforms laid the groundwork for modernizing the tax structure. GST is the most significant indirect tax reform in India, designed to eliminate the cascading effect of taxes and boost efficiency.

☛ Country that introduced GST → India
☛ Key components of GST → CGST, SGST, IGST
☛ Previous indirect taxes replaced by GST → VAT, Service Tax, Excise Duty
☛ Constitutional amendment for GST → 101st Amendment Act
